newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak c.bank not to re-impose credit limits.
newsitem.headline: Slovak c.bank not to re-impose credit limits.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovak (NBS) said on Thursday it was not planning to re-impose limits on the amount of credit commercial banks can grant to clients, a measure that was in force until the end of 1995.
"At the moment the central bank is not considering re-imposing the credit limits," NBS Governor Vladimir Masar told a news confernce.

Last month the NBS vice-governor Marian Jusko said the central bank might consider reimposing of the credit limits for commercial bank after an extensive amount of loans were extended over the past few months.
His comments sparked fears among the commercial banks over such a move.
But Masar said the NBS intented to use such administrative measures only as a last resort, and that the bank would regulate the market through its market tools. He did not elaborate.
On Wednesday, the NBS raised its bill repurchase rate by 70 basis points to 9.7 percent, but left the reverse repo rate unchanged at 7.2 percent.
Wednesday's repo hike pushed Slovak interbank money market offered rates up to the range of 13.2-14.93 percent an all maturities on Thursday.

The move also prompted dealers to question whether a hike in the Lombard rate, the NBS last-resort lending facility, might be coming soon, but Masar on Thursday did not indicate that such a move was planned.
